Override events should be logged and reviewed as safety signals, not as simple noncompliance.
Quality and safety offices should review post-deployment signals, investigate incidents, and be able to recommend reconfiguration, restriction, suspension, or withdrawal.

unlisted_practices: Schedule recurring subgroup performance reviews and equity-sensitive analysis of concerning AI output patterns.
Establish escalation pathways for AI harms that are not visible to individual clinicians in real time.
Define before deployment who reviews oversight signals, how often, and which patterns trigger audit or intervention.
Institutions should make clear that justified divergence from AI recommendations is expected, documented, and protected.
Design interface defaults so that overriding AI is not slower than complying and recommendations are not presented as mandates.
Avoid compressed decision windows when independent appraisal of AI output is required.
Build usable, auditable pause, correction, suspension, and deactivation functions and define thresholds for reconfiguration, restriction, suspension, or decommissioning.
Support frontline clinicians to document overrides, report concerns, and participate in feedback loops.
Document each oversight follow-up action and reassess whether further control is needed.
Ensure traceable generation and routing and clear responsibility for configuration rules in generative or semi-agentic patient communication systems.
